newsitem.title: USA: Chiron Q3 Betaseron revs totaled $16.8 mln.
newsitem.headline: Chiron Q3 Betaseron revs totaled $16.8 mln.

text.p: Chiron Corp said revenues from its multiple sclerosis drug Betaseron were $16.8 million in the third quarter.
Chiron resumed Betaseron shipments in the third quarter, after halting them in the second quarter.
Revenues for Betaseron were $18.5 million in the year-ago third quarter.

Chiron said its third quarter Betaseron revenues were split about evenly between initial payments for shipment of products to Berlex and secondary payments by Schering AG, which resulted from final sales of the product to customers. Berlex Labroatories is Schering's U.S. affiliate.

Chiron also said diagnostic product sales increased to $134.8 million in the third quarter from $131.2 million the year before. It said sales of bDNA probe tests, especially the tests to measure HIV viral load, were a major contributor to the overall rise, totaling $6.1 million, up from $3.3 million last year.
Ophthalmic product sales by the Chiron Vision unit rose to $49.9 million from $45.9 million the year before, mainly because of new sales from the Vitrasert Implant for CMV retinitis, Chiron said.
Oncology product sales by Chiron Therapeutics in the U.S. and Europe rose to $16.6 million from $15.8 million. Vaccine product sales rose to $21.4 million from $18.2 million.
The company reported third quarter earnings of $0.07 a share on revenues of $321.5 million compared with a net loss of $0.90 a share on revenues of $274.7 million for the third quarter of 1995.

Chiron also said diagnostic product sales increased to $134.8 million in the third quarter from $131.2 million the year before. It said sales of bDNA probe tests, especially the tests to measure HIV viral load, were a major contributor to the overall rise, totaling $6.1 million, up from $3.3 million last year.

Ophthalmic product sales by the Chiron Vision unit rose to $49.9 million from $45.9 million the year before. Most of the increase resulted from sales of the Vitrasert Implant for CMV retinitis, which was released for marketing in the U.S. in March. Sales of the Vitrasert Implant were $3.3 million in the third quarter of 1996, Chiron said.
Oncology product sales by Chiron Therapeutics in the U.S. and Europe rose to $16.6 million from $15.8 million. Vaccine product sales rose to $21.4 million from $18.2 million.
